correctness.rationale: Even sums of the original five consecutive generators are obtained using the two even generators x,x+1 and pairs of the three odd generators, reducing to x,x+1,2x−1,2x+3. For b=x+1,c=2x−1,d=2x+3, identities b+c=3x, c+d=2b+2x, and 3b=d+x reduce each Apéry factorization to either a pure c-power or d-powers plus at most two b, yielding the stated minimum formula in every residue. Subtracting branches gives x(2x−1−8q−3s) for residue r=3q+s, producing the exact cutoff R by x mod4. The standard Apéry partial order tests successors under b,c,d and yields maximal residues {R,R+1}, {R−1,R,R+1}, {R−2,R}, {R−2,R,R+1} for residues x mod4=0,1,2,3. Subtract x to obtain PF rows and type. The x=4 redundant-generator boundary is included. Fresh independent Dijkstra residue shortest-path computation, not the formula itself, verified all Apéry minima and PF maximal elements for x=4..250; finite checks do not replace the all-x normal-form proof.
residual_risks: The maximal-Apéry successor exclusion at the branch tie x≡2 mod4 is critical and was separately included in the comparison.

An older Adeniran quotient article was located indirectly but not obtained in full, leaving a specific implicit-coverage risk. No equivalent uniform Apéry and PF classification emerged in Resultary searches; this is only best-of-knowledge originality.
